subject.title: Per-account native command prefix for multi-agent slash commands

question: Should Slack multi-account native slash commands use explicit account-level `nativeNames` mapping, constrained `nativePrefix` sugar, or remain documented as unsupported for duplicate native command names?
rationale: Current main lacks the account-level naming contract, and the two closed implementation attempts show a real API/config design fork for a compatibility-sensitive Slack account surface.

options.title: Implement Explicit Native Names
options.body: Add validated per-account command-key to native-name mapping with duplicate and Slack format checks, registration, dispatch, docs, and tests.

options.title: Implement Constrained Prefix Sugar
options.body: Add a single validated lowercase prefix option if maintainers prefer simpler operator setup over per-command naming control.

options.title: Document Unsupported Duplicates
options.body: Leave runtime unchanged and document that multiple Slack apps in one workspace must not register identical native command names.

recommendation.title: Implement Explicit Native Names
recommendation.body: Add validated per-account command-key to native-name mapping with duplicate and Slack format checks, registration, dispatch, docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for the Slack native-command and shared command-registry surfaces points to this owner route.
